meta.title: Pharmy Case Study: Clinical Trial Hub | Viesigners
meta.description: How Charles-Erick BG redesigned a clinical trial application flow, A/B tested it and shaped a hub for finding nearby trials.

sections.h1: Helping people find a clinical trial *without losing them on the way*
sections.lead: A global company ran separate clinical trial microsites and wanted more qualification forms from potential participants. I helped redesign the form flow, built the A/B test around it and guided the team toward one hub to learn, find a nearby trial and apply.

brief.t: a company of about 30,000 employees focused on difficult-to-cure diseases. Pharmy is a fictional name; the real one is under NDA.
UX designer, working with the client’s strategy team and O2Web.

sections.label: The problem
prose: In the original version, 94.4% of visitors left before reaching the qualification form. The leadership team wanted more forms from potential participants.
People needed to learn about the disease and the trial process, find a nearby trial, then apply. That content was spread across separate microsites, so there were two jobs to do.

steps.p: Split the application form in two steps, redesign the microsites and measure the change with an A/B test.
Combine them in one hub where people gain knowledge and find the closest trials for their condition.

sections.label: Approach
prose: I worked closely with the client’s strategy team to define target user profiles and the indicators that mattered, then wrote the A/B test methodology and measurement plan. I also made sure the measuring tools were in place.
I guided the project team through inspiration, ideation, prototyping and technical validation, with wireframes in Axure and analytics from Google Analytics and Hotjar.

sections.label: What real users did
sections.h2: What the A/B test *showed, and what it didn’t*

results.t: higher share of visitors reached the qualification form, from 5.6% to 8.3%
completed forms on 770 and 640 visits, from 1.95% to 2.34%
version B completions were prequalified candidates

sections.caption: Funnel by version
head: Stage
Version A
Version B

reads.p: Version B moved more visitors to the form, a borderline result on this sample (p≈0.045). It also separated qualified candidates from everyone else, which version A couldn’t do.

With 15 completions on each side, the overall lift isn’t conclusive (p≈0.61). Confirming it would take about 22,000 visits per version. A smaller share of the people who reached the form finished it, so the next step would have been to study that drop.

Version B changed the form and the design at the same time, so this test can’t credit either one alone. Traffic was also uneven, with 770 and 640 visits. [À FOURNIR : test dates, analytics source and anything else that changed in that period]
